napoleon.title: Napoleon = Joseph Stalin
napoleon.text: Napoleon is a large, fierce-looking Berkshire boar who represents Joseph Stalin. Although he initially supports the rebellion's promise of equality, he gradually becomes a ruthless dictator. His expulsion of Snowball mirrors Stalin's removal of Leon Trotsky, while his trained dogs represent the secret police used to intimidate opponents. Through Squealer's propaganda and changes to the Seven Commandments, Napoleon manipulates the animals and justifies his privileges. His eventual resemblance to the human farmers reveals how completely he has betrayed the revolution.

snowball.title: Snowball = Leon Trotsky
snowball.text: Snowball is an intelligent pig who represents Leon Trotsky. He helps lead the rebellion and proposes improvements, including the windmill, which he believes will make life easier for the animals. His struggle with Napoleon reflects the rivalry between Trotsky and Stalin after Lenin's death. When Napoleon uses his dogs to drive Snowball away, this mirrors Trotsky's exile. Napoleon later blames Snowball for the farm's problems, just as Stalin portrayed Trotsky as an enemy of the Soviet Union.

squealer.title: Squealer = Soviet propaganda
squealer.text: Squealer is a persuasive pig who represents Soviet propaganda and the state-controlled press. He uses misleading statistics, fear, and carefully chosen language to defend Napoleon's decisions. Whenever the pigs contradict the principles of Animalism, Squealer convinces the animals that these changes are necessary for their own good. Through Squealer, Orwell demonstrates how propaganda can distort reality and persuade people to accept their own exploitation.

boxer.title: Boxer = the loyal working class
boxer.text: Boxer is a powerful, devoted horse who represents the exploited working class. His determination to work harder makes him essential to the farm, especially during the construction of the windmill. However, his belief that Napoleon is always right prevents him from recognizing how the pigs manipulate him. When he becomes too weak to work, Napoleon sells him to a horse slaughterer rather than providing the retirement he was promised. Through him, Orwell shows how honest labor and devotion can be exploited when they are not accompanied by critical questioning.

clover.title: Clover = the people who half-remember
clover.text: Clover, the motherly cart-horse, represents ordinary Soviet citizens: loyal, hard-working, and slowly aware that something is wrong. She half-remembers the original Commandments and asks Muriel to read them, but cannot bring herself to believe the leaders would lie. After the executions she looks out over the farm and thinks: this is not what we aimed at - yet she cannot put it into words, so she keeps working. Orwell gives her the closest thing the book has to a conscience, and shows that a conscience without power changes nothing.

benjamin.title: Benjamin = the silent cynic
benjamin.text: Benjamin the donkey is the oldest animal and reads as well as any pig. He believes nothing ever really changes - 'Donkeys live a long time' - and refuses to take sides. Many readers see him as the intellectuals who understood what Stalin was doing but stayed silent; some see a little of Orwell himself: sceptical, never fooled, but not acting. You are playing him. Notice how much he sees, and how little he says.

moses.title: Moses = the Russian Orthodox Church
moses.text: Moses the raven represents organized religion, particularly the Russian Orthodox Church. His stories about Sugarcandy Mountain promise the animals a peaceful afterlife where their suffering will end. These promises offer comfort but can also encourage them to endure injustice rather than challenge it. Although the pigs initially reject Moses, they later tolerate him, suggesting that rulers may support religion when it helps keep the population obedient.

muriel.title: Muriel = the literate who do not act
muriel.text: Muriel is a literate goat who represents ordinary people with enough education to recognize signs of deception but limited power to oppose it. She reads the commandments for the other animals and helps them investigate changes to the rules but ultimately she is overwhelmed by fear.

sheep.title: The sheep = the unthinking crowd
sheep.text: The sheep represent unquestioning followers who repeat political slogans without understanding them. Their chanting reduces complicated ideas to simple phrases and prevents meaningful discussion. Because the pigs can easily teach them new slogans, the sheep become a tool for silencing criticism.

hen.title: The hens = peasants who resisted
hen.text: The hens represent peasants who resisted Stalin and died. When Napoleon orders them to surrender their eggs for sale, they rebel rather than give up what they have produced. He responds by withholding their food, causing several hens to die. Their suffering reflects the brutal treatment of those who resisted state control of agricultural production and exposes the violence beneath Napoleon's claims to serve all animals.

dog.title: The dogs = the secret police (NKVD or KGB)
dog.text: The dogs represent Stalin's secret police, who protected his authority through surveillance, intimidation, and violence. Napoleon takes them away as puppies and raises them to obey him. They drive Snowball from the farm and carry out Napoleon's executions, resembling the repression and purges under Stalin.

puppy.title: The dogs = the secret police (NKVD or KGB)
puppy.text: The dogs represent Stalin's secret police, who protected his authority through surveillance, intimidation, and violence. Napoleon takes them away as puppies and raises them to obey him. They drive Snowball from the farm and carry out Napoleon's executions, resembling the repression and purges under Stalin.

pig.title: The pigs = the privileged Soviet ruling class
pig.text: The pigs as a group represent the Bolshevik leadership and the privileged Soviet ruling class that develops after the revolution. Their intelligence allows them to organize the rebellion, but they gradually use their authority to claim special treatment. By controlling education, food, and information, they place themselves above the other animals.

cow.title: The milk = the first theft
cow.text: The cows represent working producers whose resources are taken by the ruling class. Their milk is reserved for the pigs instead of being shared among the animals. This early inequality reveals that the new leaders are already placing their own comfort above the revolution's promises.

commandments.title: The Seven Commandments = the revolution's ideals
commandments.text: The Seven Commandments represent the revolution's founding principles of equality and the socialist ideals it claims to uphold. Initially, they provide rules intended to prevent animals from behaving like their human oppressors. As the pigs gain power, the commandments are secretly altered to excuse their actions. Eventually, the rules are reduced to a declaration that preserves the language of equality while openly permitting inequality.

flag.title: The flag = the Soviet flag
flag.text: The flagpole and the flag symbolize the revolution's shared identity and its promises of unity. The flag's hoof and horn resemble the Soviet hammer and sickle, replacing the symbols of human workers with those of animals. Ceremonies around the flag encourage loyalty to Animal Farm, even as its leaders betray the principles it originally represented.

windmill.title: The windmill = Soviet industrialisation
windmill.text: The windmill represents Soviet industrialization. It is presented as a project that will reduce labor and bring prosperity, encouraging the animals to make enormous sacrifices. Instead, its construction brings exhausting work and hardship while strengthening the pigs' control. Napoleon first rejects Snowball's proposal and later claims it as his own, demonstrating how leaders can rewrite the past to take credit for others' ideas. The windmill ultimately illustrates how promises of future progress can be used to justify suffering in the present.

farmhouse.title: The farmhouse = the Kremlin
farmhouse.text: The farmhouse symbolizes the wealth, privilege, and separation of the ruling class. At first, the animals agree that no one should live there, since it represents Jones's comfortable life at their expense. When the pigs move in and adopt human habits, they take over the privileges they once condemned.
